8:

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.

content.text:
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

  goto <url>                  navigate to a url

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording

  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions

  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:

## Objective
- Add event-specific imagery to the investigation game, including the discovery of a corpse and a photograph taken at the crime scene.

## Requirements
- Images should correspond to investigation events.

## Decisions
- Use locally stored SVG illustrations for a non-graphic crime-scene reconstruction and scene evidence photograph.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `images/mara-found.svg` and `images/scene-photograph.svg`.
- Added crime-scene imagery to the scene interaction modal and linked it to “A bell after the storm” and “Scene documented” timeline events.
- Added timeline image styling in `style.css`.
- Previously updated camera follow behavior while retaining 30% zoom; `node --check game.js` passed at that time.
- Previously tested investigation interactions, evidence collection, warrant approval and execution, Crowe’s detention, and the “A case, not a confession” ending.

### Active
- Validate the new image and timeline changes; no validation has been run since these edits.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js` and inspect the modified rendering and scene-photograph flow.
2. If practical, visually check the timeline and scene modal.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Event imagery mapping, timeline rendering, and scene interaction.
- `style.css`: Scene and event image presentation.
- `images/mara-found.svg`: Non-graphic discovery scene reconstruction.
- `images/scene-photograph.svg`: Stylized scene evidence photograph.

## Important Context
- `S.events` entries can include an `image` field; existing “A bell after the storm” events are handled by title fallback.
- Photographing the scene sets `S.flags.scenePhoto` and adds a “Scene documented” event with `image:'scene-photo'`.
- Work is uncommitted.

Identify relevant functions/files and any existing clues, case-file tabs, action patterns. Do not edit files.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e2ae79698ffe6eExWrjxikyGZ6" state="completed">
## Existing detective interactions

- **Primary interaction loop:** `interact()` checks the nearby location and calls `actPlace(p)`. `actPlace()` routes to location-specific modals, where investigation actions are supplied as buttons with callbacks. See [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L75) and [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L121).
- **Input and navigation:** Players use **E** or the touch **INTERACT** button; case-file access is available through **Q**, the sidebar button, or touch controls. Sidebar lead cards set a route to a location, while person rows open a person modal. See [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L124) and [`index.html`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html#L26).
- **Location actions:** The scene offers evidence collection and photography; the diner and church have interview/record actions; the morgue offers a preliminary report; the archive, apartment, hospital, and other locations provide leads, interviews, searches, or recovery/rest actions. Most actions record evidence or events, advance time, and update/save state.
- **Evidence catalog:** `evidenceData` defines the split-halo mark, gray wool fiber, choir token, Jonah’s witness account, the Ninth Verse, estimated time of death, restricted register, and Mara’s unsent letter. These entries include descriptions and evidence classifications. See [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L23).
- **Case-file tabs:** `caseFile()` builds **Overview, Evidence, People, Timeline, Theories,** and **Saves**. The theories tab currently displays a fixed checklist of four clue links, marked “supported lead” or “needs corroboration”; it has no player action. See [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L105).
- **Warrant action:** The precinct compares evidence and gates the warrant behind a set of evidence and interview requirements. The precinct already has a “pin evidence” action, but it shows a fixed analysis rather than asking the player to make a connection. See [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L81).

## Focused improvement

**Make the existing Theories tab an interactive “review this link” panel.** Keep its four current theory prompts, but let the player open each one to inspect the specific evidence behind it, including relevant caveats, and choose to record it as a *working link* in the existing `S.theories` array. For example, reviewing the parish-imagery link could show the scene mark and ledger entry while reiterating that their connection does not identify a killer.

This is a contained change to the existing case-file UI and state: it turns a passive checklist into a detective decision, reuses the established evidence descriptions and modal/action-button pattern, and can leave the warrant rules and overall architecture unchanged. No files were edited.
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Make the game more interactive around its detective feature while preserving event-specific imagery for the corpse discovery and crime-scene photograph.

## Requirements
- Investigation imagery should correspond to events.
- Detective interactions should help players test clue connections without presenting theories as proof.

## Decisions
- Use local SVG illustrations for a non-graphic crime-scene reconstruction and scene photograph.
- Add a precinct evidence board where players select and test clue connections, with feedback for support, timeline tension, and unresolved links.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `images/mara-found.svg` and `images/scene-photograph.svg`, linked to timeline events and the scene interaction modal.
- Added a selectable two-to-three-clue case board; tested connections are saved in `S.theories` and displayed in the case-file theories view.
- Added board-selection and feedback styling.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify board selection, feedback, saved theory display, and responsive presentation in a browser.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has no result: Chromium’s first headless run crashed; a later run returned the fixture’s initial `STARTING` state without executing the test. Selenium is unavailable (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'selenium'`).

## Next Move
1. Run the board interaction test in a working browser automation setup and report pass/fail.
2. Check the board and event imagery at a narrow viewport.
3. Review any issues and rerun `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Investigation actions, evidence board, case-file tabs, event imagery, and theory logic.
- `style.css`: Modal, case-file, and evidence-board presentation.
- `images/mara-found.svg`: Non-graphic discovery scene illustration.
- `images/scene-photograph.svg`: Stylized scene evidence photograph.
- `/tmp/opencode-detective-fixture.py`: Temporary browser-test fixture for the case-board flow.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing detective features include location-based investigation actions, evidence collection, interviews, leads, and a case-file theories view.
- `S.events` supports an `image` field; “A bell after the storm” has a title fallback for older saves.
- Photographing the scene sets `S.flags.scenePhoto` and adds a “Scene documented” event with `image:'scene-photo'`.
- Case-board combinations currently map to fixed feedback: `sigil` + `ledger`, `witness` + `autopsy`, `register` + `letter`, and `fiber` + `token`; other combinations are unresolved.
- The board stores up to 12 theory records, keyed by selected clue set.

## Objective
- Make the game more interactive around its detective feature while preserving event-specific imagery for the corpse discovery and crime-scene photograph.
- Let players test clue connections without presenting theories as proof.

## Requirements
- Investigation imagery should correspond to events.
- Detective interactions should help players test clue connections without presenting theories as proof.

## Decisions
- Use local SVG illustrations for a non-graphic crime-scene reconstruction and scene photograph.
- Add a precinct evidence board where players select and test clue connections, with feedback for support, timeline tension, and unresolved links.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `images/mara-found.svg` and `images/scene-photograph.svg`, linked to timeline events and the scene interaction modal.
- Added a selectable two-to-three-clue case board; tested connections are saved in `S.theories` and displayed in the case-file theories view.
- Added board-selection and feedback styling.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Resolve the browser-test runtime error, then verify board selection, feedback, saved theory display, and narrow-screen presentation.

### Blocked
- Browser test fails before the precinct modal opens with `PAGE ERROR Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'precinct')`; no interaction or responsive checks completed.

## Next Move
1. Diagnose the `undefined (reading 'precinct')` runtime error in the browser test.
2. Rerun the board interaction and saved-theory flow in Chromium.
3. Check board presentation at a narrow viewport and rerun `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Investigation actions, evidence board, case-file tabs, event imagery, and theory logic.
- `style.css`: Modal, case-file, and evidence-board presentation.
- `images/mara-found.svg`: Non-graphic discovery scene illustration.
- `images/scene-photograph.svg`: Stylized scene evidence photograph.
- `/tmp/opencode-detective-fixture.py`: Temporary browser-test fixture for the case-board flow.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed modified `game.js` and `style.css`, plus untracked `images/`.
- `S.events` supports an `image` field; “A bell after the storm” has a title fallback for older saves.
- Photographing the scene sets `S.flags.scenePhoto` and adds a “Scene documented” event with `image:'scene-photo'`.
- Case-board combinations currently map to fixed feedback: `sigil` + `ledger`, `witness` + `autopsy`, `register` + `letter`, and `fiber` + `token`; other combinations are unresolved.
- The board stores up to 12 theory records, keyed by selected clue set.
